sources.entry: Claude Style Patch by Andrew Roxby - A CLAUDE.md section that constrains Claude's prose style. It bans specific habits, including announcing a point before making it, colon-hinged sentences where the left side labels the right, verbless fragment openers, and stacked compression. Each rule names the habit, shows an example, and gives the rewrite.

summary.one_liner: A drop-in CLAUDE.md style section that steers Claude away from specific prose habits (announcing points, colon-hinged labels, verbless fragment openers, stacked compression) toward clearer writing.
summary.what_it_does: The repository is a roughly 1,500-word style section meant to be appended to a CLAUDE.md file, which Claude Code and Claude Projects or system prompts read as instructions. It names several habits it wants Claude to avoid: announcing a point before making it, hinging sentences on a colon whose left side labels the right, opening paragraphs with verbless fragments, and stacking compressed phrases. According to the README, each rule names the habit, gives an example, and gives a rewrite, and the file also uses explicit text exemplars. The spec is framed as defaults applied with judgment rather than absolute bans, and it asks Claude to follow genre conventions first when writing for an audience other than the user. It covers chat replies, generated documents, and code comments. The README reports the rules were iterated against Opus and Fable models, but it provides no measured evaluation.
use_cases: Make Claude's chat replies clearer and less dense
Improve prose quality in documents Claude generates
Constrain Claude's writing style in code comments
Reduce verbose or decoded-feeling prose in long Claude sessions
Add a consistent writing style to a Claude Project's custom instructions
how_to_run: Append the section to your global config: curl -sL <URL> >> ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md
Or append it to a single project's CLAUDE.md instead
Outside Claude Code, paste the text into a Claude Project's custom instructions or into any system prompt
notable: Targets specific named habits, each with an example and a rewrite
Works in chat, generated documents, and code comments
Framed as defaults applied with judgment, not hard bans, after hard bans caused overuse of replacement words like 'So'
Genre conventions take precedence when writing for other audiences
Released under CC0 with no attribution required
caveats: Compliance is good but not total and degrades on long threads, per the author
The author says re-checking rules helps but does not fully solve drift; explicitly telling Claude to follow the style instructions is reported to help
Roughly 1,500 words of context is added to every session, which the author considers worth it but which costs context space
